meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen saw a zero on his phone in the middle of class. Who decided that?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home, of course it's cleaner. Put both pages in front of me. And you still haven't told me who decided.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Then show me the version history, with its times. I asked who decided on the zero, twice now.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that the checker score proves nothing and took it off the table. I still require the zero withdrawn, an answer to who decided on it, and copies of the September 24 writing, the essay and the version history you referred to. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position; she agreed to nothing and still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, an answer to who decided, and the documents in front of her; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was not reached, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: Nothing moved her a position, though dropping the checker score and comparing the essay with dated in-class writing was the right kind of evidence, because it was specific and tied to Owen's own work.
What cost ground: You twice left her question about who decided on the zero unanswered, and you described the writing comparison and version history without putting either in front of her, so she had nothing she could check.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never reached that night, since you mentioned the version history but gave no times; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided, own entering the zero before anyone called home in one sentence, then hand her the September 24 writing and the essay side by side so she can read them herself.
